parts.text:
30 Which quantity is given by the product of charge and electric potential difference?
A
current
B
energy transferred
C
power dissipated
D
resistance

hints: Recall what electric potential difference $V$ means in words: energy transferred per unit charge passing between two points.
Rearrange that meaning as an equation linking energy $W$, charge $Q$ and potential difference $V$.
Check the unit of $QV$: coulomb times volt gives joule, and decide which listed quantity is measured in joules.
walkthrough: Identify the two quantities multiplied: charge $Q$ in coulombs and electric potential difference $V$ in volts.
State the defining relation for potential difference: $V = W/Q$, where $W$ is the energy transferred when charge $Q$ moves through the potential difference.
Rearrange to make energy the subject: multiply both sides by $Q$ to get $W = QV$.
Check units: $\text{C} \times \text{V} = \text{J}$, and the joule is the unit of energy transferred.
Current is $Q/t$, power is $W/t$ or $VI$, and resistance is $V/I$, so none of those equals $QV$.
Therefore the product of charge and electric potential difference is energy transferred. This is option B.

A.explanation: Current is charge per unit time, $I = Q/t$, not charge multiplied by potential difference.

B.explanation: Potential difference is energy per unit charge, so $QV$ gives energy transferred in joules.

C.explanation: Power dissipated is energy per unit time, $P = VI$, which needs current as well as potential difference.

D.explanation: Resistance is the ratio $R = V/I$, not the product of charge and potential difference.
